cues.show: You with the guitar, the riff's tab on screen.
cues.say: A riff is a short line that repeats. This one is written out note by note.

cues.show: Press the Play button and listen, hands off the guitar.
cues.say: Press the Play button below and just listen. Hum along until you can hum the riff before it plays.

cues.show: Stop. Play the first few notes alone, slowly, fretting hand visible.
cues.say: Now learn it in pieces. Play only the first few notes, slowly, and say which finger goes where.

cues.show: Stop. Play the first few notes alone, slowly, fretting hand visible.
cues.say: When those come easily, add the next few.

cues.show: Use − under Tempo, press Play, and play along.
cues.say: Under Tempo, press the minus button to slow it down. Then press Play and play along.

cues.show: Use − under Tempo, press Play, and play along.
cues.say: The notes are spaced by how long they last, so a wide gap is a long note.

cues.show: Play it from memory with the tool, eyes on the guitar.
cues.say: Practice until you can play the riff with your eyes on the guitar and not on the screen.

cues.show: Play it muted, then louder, then an octave up or on other strings.
cues.say: Try things with it. Rest the side of your picking hand on the strings by the bridge and play it muted.

cues.show: Play it muted, then louder, then an octave up or on other strings.
cues.say: Play it with only down strokes, then with down and up.

cues.show: Play it muted, then louder, then an octave up or on other strings.
cues.say: Find the same notes somewhere else on the neck and play the riff there.

cues.show: Play it muted, then louder, then an octave up or on other strings.
cues.say: Then change the last two notes and make it your own.
